newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks close higher on Dow's rebound.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks close higher on Dow's rebound.

text.p: * Index to trade within 3,130 to 3,200 for the week
Selective buying, mostly in index heavyweights, propelled the market up at close on Monday as investors found inspiration in the Dow's rebound, traders said.
"With the Dow's strength, investors are looking at our market for opportunities and they are hungry for good stocks," said Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities.
The main index closed 17.11 points up, or 0.54 percent, at 3,186.37 points.
"Inflation figures were treated positively by the market," said Erwin Tan, research manager at Abacus Securities Cor.

He said market expectations that the government would meet its full-year inflation inflation target of 7.5 to 8.7 percent was confirmed. The National Statistics Office announced that 1996 full-year inflation was at 8.4 percent.
The listing of PCI Leasing and Finance Inc shares also gave the market a boost when it opened up at 7.60 pesos from an offering price of 6.95 pesos.
PCI Leasing was the most actively traded issue, ending at 7.50 pesos a share.
Value turnover was modest at 1.685 billion pesos with 4.342 billion shares traded. All sectors were up with the oil and finance sector bucking the trend.
Gainers outpaced decliners 61 to 50 with 66 issues unchanged.
Traders said there may be some selling in PCI Leasing on Tuesday owing to its gains today before any follow-through buying could continue.
"There's no compelling reason for the market to fly so the market may move sideways for the rest of the week," Tan said.
